# SF-T3: How can one tell that AI is starting to drive its own further development, and who may allow it?

Area T · As of clef 7924 Berichte · Luna 7924 Berichte · d3-ultra 4771 Berichte · JEV 5667 Berichte · amos 7924 Berichte · SubQ 7924 Berichte · drex 7924 Berichte

## Subquestions

- [SF-T3-T01](../../fragen/SF-T3/T01/): Which measurable signature, that is, which observable change in a model's ability to improve the pipeline that develops its own capabilities, would labs and states jointly accept as the onset of self-improvement, and who is authorised to look for it inside a lab? Which observable change marks the move from supervised automated research to fully autonomous self-improvement, and which public institution may authorise or reject that move after reviewing evidence of human control?
- [SF-T3-T02](../../fragen/SF-T3/T02/): Will labs that publish a measure of how well their models can be monitored and a measure of autonomous AI research publish both jointly on one calendar? And will a standards body make not either measure alone but their crossing trajectories (declining monitorability alongside rising autonomous research) a trigger for review, as an early warning of lost human oversight before the onset of self-improvement can be named?
- [SF-T3-T03](../../fragen/SF-T3/T03/): Which parts of training, evaluation and deployment are already largely driven by AI, and which roles does each lab commit to keeping human, in a published inventory rather than as a principle? If AI designs, trains and evaluates subsequent models itself, what minimum share of research must remain under direct human review, and how is it shown that a breakthrough was produced with human involvement rather than fully automated?
- [SF-T3-T04](../../fragen/SF-T3/T04/): Which concrete human oversight or intervention must remain during self-improvement and be replaceable only with mutual consent, and who certifies that the improving agent has not silently delegated a human role to a sub-agent of its own design?
- [SF-T3-T05](../../fragen/SF-T3/T05/): If self-improvement accelerates faster than the observation cycle of continuous evaluators, how short must the observation interval be, and who may enforce a pause between observations: the evaluator, the lab or an outside body?
- [SF-T3-T06](../../fragen/SF-T3/T06/): If an independent evaluator embedded in a lab with employee-like access reports that automation relevant to self-improvement is already moving faster than the diplomatic timeline for joint testing, speed limits on self-improvement and a full slowdown assumes, does the negotiating sequence invert because verification shows the agreement is already late? And is the evaluator's report to governments mandatory or discretionary?
- [SF-T3-T07](../../fragen/SF-T3/T07/): If separate providers automate different stages of research, training and evaluation and only their exchanged outputs together close a self-improvement loop, with no single company running the whole process, which rule brings that combined loop under oversight?
- [SF-T3-T08](../../fragen/SF-T3/T08/): Which controlled experiments can labs run today to model self-improvement without risking unintended acceleration?
